test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 17 March, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

He said, “You were making excuses.”

options.text: He said that I had been making excuses.
He said that you were making excuses.
He said that you had been making excuses.
He said that I was making excuses.

solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **correct indirect form** of the given sentence is **option 1: **"He said that I had been making excuses."
 
• In reported speech, if the reporting verb (like "said" in this case) is in the past tense, then **we usually shift the tenses back **in the reported clause.
 
• When, the given direct sentence is in **'Past continuous tense'** , the indirect sentence will be** changed** to **'Past perfect continuous tense'**.
 
• **'Were' **will be changed into **'Had been'.**
 
• **'You'** will be changed into **'I'.**

Therefore, the **correct answer** is:* 'He said that I had been making excuses.'*
